title: Krakatoa’s 1883 blast was heard nearly 5,000 km away
body: On 27 August 1883 the Indonesian volcano Krakatoa exploded so violently that people on Rodrigues, an island near Mauritius about 4,800 km away, thought they were hearing distant cannon fire. It is considered the loudest sound in recorded history. The eruption collapsed most of the island, and it and the tsunamis it caused killed at least 36,000 people.

slides.heading: Around the world 3.5 times
slides.text: Barographs worldwide recorded the pressure wave as many as seven times over five days, as it raced to the far side of the planet and back.

slides.heading: Fire engines in New York
slides.text: Volcanic haze made sunsets so vividly red that fire engines were called out in New York and New Haven to fight fires that weren’t there.

slides.heading: A cooler summer
slides.text: In the year after the eruption, average summer temperatures in the Northern Hemisphere fell by about 0.4 °C as volcanic particles reflected sunlight.
